mainEntity.name: How does pricing work for electrical troubleshooting in Falls Church, VA?

acceptedAnswer.text: We come to the house, look at the actual work, and give a written estimate before any repair starts. Diagnostic visits include most minor on-the-spot repairs. Major repairs get a separate written estimate. No charge for the diagnostic visit in our primary service area.

mainEntity.name: How quickly can you come out for a troubleshooting call in Falls Church?

acceptedAnswer.text: Same-day or next-day in most cases during weekday business hours. Falls Church is about 5 miles from our Fairfax Blvd office — roughly 10–15 minutes via Route 29 or Route 50. If your situation is urgent — burning smell, sparking, warm walls — we will triage you to the earliest available slot and tell you what to shut off in the meantime.

mainEntity.name: What is included in a troubleshooting visit?

acceptedAnswer.text: A real diagnostic — not a guess. We use a multimeter, circuit tracer, AFCI/GFCI tester, and IR thermal camera if heat is suspected. We open panels, test circuits at rest and under load, trace the fault to its source, then explain what we found in plain English before any repair starts.

mainEntity.name: When should I call an electrician versus trying to fix it myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: Call an electrician if you smell burning, see sparking, feel warm walls or warm switch plates, have a breaker that trips daily, or have lost power to part of the house without a clear cause. Resetting a tripped breaker once is fine. Resetting it three times in a row is a fire risk.

mainEntity.name: What is the most common electrical problem in Falls Church homes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Breaker trips on overloaded circuits. Falls Church's housing stock is dominated by 1940s–1970s construction — from brick Cape Cods in Greenway Downs with original 60-amp fuse boxes, to 1960s split-levels in Broadmont and Madison Manor with 100-amp panels, to expanded ramblers in Pimmit Hills where additions were wired without upgrading the service. These homes were never designed for central AC, multiple kitchen appliances, home offices, and EV chargers. The second most common call is flickering lights — usually a loose neutral at the meter base or voltage drop from an aging Dominion Energy service connection.

mainEntity.name: Do you handle EV charger problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. EV charging puts continuous high-amp draw on circuits that Falls Church's mid-century homes were not wired for. If your charger throttles, trips a breaker, or warms the outlet, the cause is almost always upstream — a feeder, a breaker, or a connection that cannot sustain the load. We diagnose the cause and either repair it or quote you for the right circuit.
